Market stance

Friday’s tape split the group between a confirmed cyber/software bid (Remz, with ZS, NET and PANW all up over 7% on heavy volume) and a bottom-calling camp (Enrich: “we bottom very soon”) heading into Prof’s blockbuster earnings-and-FOMC week, while Sean preached patience through the correction and iain posted no trades at all.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • MSFT · GOOGL · AMZN earnings next week (plus $SKHY $NOW $INTC $SNDK $TWLO)
  • FOMC + Jobless Claims + PCE + GDP
  • Weekend geopolitical risks: US–Iran, Russia–Ukraine (Prof)
  • Fear & Greed 21 — extreme fear (Prof)

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Friday was a split tape, not a rout: the indexes drifted lower on quiet volume (SPY −0.52% on 0.82x volume, QQQ flat) while software and cyber exploded — Remz’s “relentlessly bid up” call, confirmed in price. The group’s camps are now bottom-callers (Enrich: “we bottom very soon”, Santa rally next) and process-first patience (Sean: corrections build the next opportunities; iain: no trades missed, weekend at the cabin; Prof: follow a process, don’t blindly follow perma bulls or bears) — with DiCarlo the only one actively exiting positions (TE, CIFR sold). Your process sides with patience until price confirms: the cyber follow-through names are watches with named lines, not chases, and the failed-zone exits are a warning about this tape, not a reason to force trades.

More from the group

From the group

Sean — the correction sermon: “The market going down should EXCITE you. Corrections are where the next great opportunities are built. Weak hands get flushed out. Extended names reset. New bases start forming. The best opportunities usually come AFTER the correction.” Also: “More money won’t make you a better trader — if you can’t trade a $10,000 account, you can’t trade a $1,000,000 account.” And a bag-holding confession from 2021 (“I flipped a few thousand dollars into hundreds of thousands trading. Then I lost it all because I kept bag holding”) — process posts, no tickers.

iain — no trades, no FOMO: “I didn’t miss a single thing in the market today, and I’m content” — weekend at the cabin with family. Plus a warning that fits this tape: “The loudest traders on X always have the hottest takes & endless winning trades, yet somehow 0 proof of consistent long-term P&L or drawdowns. A good marketer isn’t automatically a good trader.” No tickers, no levels.

Enrich — zoom out: “Nothing helps me more during volatile weeks than zooming out. Daily, weekly, even monthly charts. Find the major levels. Look at the bigger trend. Higher timeframes carry more weight for me.” Plus: “Earnings szn is now underway & next week is flooded with them — chop during the day, overnight movement.” His bottom calls (“we bottom very soon”, Santa rally) are in the SPY panel.

Prof — the blockbuster week: “Next week is gonna be a blockbuster. Earnings: $MSFT $GOOGL $AMZN $SKHY $NOW $INTC $SNDK $TWLO. Economic: FOMC, Jobless Claims, PCE, GDP. Weekend geopolitical risks: US–Iran war, Russia–Ukraine war.” Plus the process post: “Follow a process. Manage your risk better. Keep your emotions in check. Don’t blindly follow perma bulls or bears.” And Fear & Greed 21, extreme fear.

Venu — stay in the game: “One thing I’ve learned in the markets is that staying in the game matters more than anything else! Recent selloffs may push quite a few people to quit the market, but it’s important to remember how rewarding the April–September 2025 and April–June 2026 runs were.” His MSFT FCF post is in the MSFT panel.

DiCarlo — three videos, two exits: WM (the A+ setup that held), TE (failed zone, moving on) and CIFR (failed zone, sold out) — all three are rows above; the videos carry the zone detail the post text doesn’t state.

Sources & Methodology
  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. All seven accounts were readable this window (top ~5 posts visible per account before the login wall).
  • Posts window: Fri Oct 23 – Sat Oct 24, 2026 — everything visible after the Oct 23 feed’s window (which ended Oct 23, 03:31 UTC). Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; two posts are truncated in the extraction itself (Remz’s SPX post, Sean’s correction post) and are quoted only to the visible cutoff.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Fri Oct 23, 2026 close. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader’s framing, and it’s labeled every time.
  • Sector lines: each card’s sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 23, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL→XLK, MSFT→IGV, NVDA→SMH, GOOGL/META→XLC, AMZN/TSLA→XLY, ZS/NET/PANW→CIBR (cybersecurity — best fit for the cyber bid), WM→XLI, TE→XLU, CIFR→IBIT (spot bitcoin as the mining proxy — best-fit choice).
  • Where none of the seven commented, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” That was QQQ (no direct mention), IWM and TLT this window; SPY is the only index with a direct trader signal (Remz’s SPX 7620).
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). Flagged follow-through watches: NET (trigger = break of Friday’s high 328.00), PANW (trigger = 381.49) — watches, not confirmed breakouts. Explicitly not qualifiers: ZS (extended, 27% above the 50-day EMA), WM (extended, +20% in three weeks from the zone), TE and CIFR (failed setups, trader sold), TSLA and GOOGL (repair-only below trend), AAPL (holds-only at the highs). MSFT is intact into earnings, not a breakout setup.
  • Coverage note: names Prof mentioned only as earnings dates ($SKHY $NOW $INTC $SNDK $TWLO) appear as catalysts, not rows — an earnings date is not a setup call. NOW was a row yesterday on Enrich’s watchlist; it is not carried over, because this window’s posts don’t repeat the call.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. Stage lives in the pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) and is kept out of the prose and the setup badges; traders’ own quoted words are exempt. Two trend reads changed from yesterday: GOOGL closed below its 50-week EMA, and AMZN slipped below its 30-week MA.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition — no trader-posted chart images were retrievable from the visible posts (DiCarlo’s and Remz’s posts link to videos; Prof’s image is a Fear & Greed screenshot, not a chart). Our charts are generated from Yahoo data, with the verification gate below.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line’s endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all 51 checks (17 symbols × 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA) passed within 0.5%, most within 0.002%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
